Evidence from Malaysia official corpus: BTR/CRT national accounting and NSRF corporate Scope accounting are both operational, while NRES states that RUU PIN is intended to introduce uniform GHG calculation methodologies across sectors.
Documentary state at cutoff: Partial: multiple valid accounting layers exist, but a binding crosswalk spanning national, facility and corporate methods is not yet evidenced.
Comparator mechanism documented elsewher: China uses sector-specific ETS accounting guides; Japan uses statutory calculation manuals; Singapore embeds calculation requirements in facility MRV regulations.
Institutional design option surfaced by: A policy design option is a formally versioned crosswalk linking national inventory, sector/facility methods and corporate Scope definitions.

Evidence from Malaysia official corpus: Energy Commission publishes regional grid emission factors and recalculates earlier values when updated data become available; BTR accounting also uses sector/IPCC factor structures.
Documentary state at cutoff: Partial: official factor sources exist, but the corpus does not evidence one national, version-controlled factor library used across all reporting layers.
Comparator mechanism documented elsewher: Japan maintains official factor lists for statutory reporting; South Korea verifies country-specific factors; India maintains a versioned CEA grid database.
Institutional design option surfaced by: A policy design option is a common factor register with provenance, effective dates, revision history and approved use cases.

Evidence from Malaysia official corpus: BTR1 is subject to UNFCCC technical expert review; NSRF reasonable assurance for Scope 1/2 begins only from 2028-2030; RUU PIN envisages accredited external auditors for industry reports.
Documentary state at cutoff: Partial/phased: national review exists, but routine independent assurance of corporate/facility emissions is not yet universal.
Comparator mechanism documented elsewher: Singapore codifies accredited external verification; South Korea requires verified emitter statements; China has sector verification guides and provincial verification.
Institutional design option surfaced by: A policy design option is a common verifier competence, independence and accreditation architecture across statutory facility MRV and corporate assurance.

Evidence from Malaysia official corpus: NSRF establishes corporate Scope 1/2/3 reporting while proposed RUU PIN establishes facility-level industry reporting. The corpus does not yet show a common identifier and reconciliation protocol between these layers.
Documentary state at cutoff: Partial: both layers are specified, but their consolidation logic is not yet integrated in an operative national system.
Comparator mechanism documented elsewher: Korea and Singapore use facility-level compliance statements as clearly defined regulatory data objects; China applies facility/enterprise reporting templates within its ETS platform.
Institutional design option surfaced by: A policy design option is a common facility identifier, organisational-consolidation rule and reconciliation control for Scope 1 totals.

Evidence from Malaysia official corpus: NRES policy documents call for a national information platform and for development/operationalisation of a national carbon registry; current UNFCCC, open-data and corporate reporting channels remain separate.
Documentary state at cutoff: Developing: the integrated registry/platform is an announced architecture rather than a completed nationwide operating backbone.
Comparator mechanism documented elsewher: China links management platform and registry systems; Korea NGMS is linked to the emissions-trading registry; Singapore uses EDMA; India has designated the ICM Registry but the compliance cycle remains recent.
Institutional design option surfaced by: A policy design option is interoperable rather than duplicated infrastructure, with traceable data lineage from source report through verification to registry use.

Evidence from Malaysia official corpus: NRES describes MRV as the basis for carbon pricing and a later ETS; the National Carbon Market Policy also connects MRV integrity and registry development to market architecture.
Documentary state at cutoff: Developing: the intended link is explicit, but a fully operational national facility-MRV-to-pricing feedback loop is not yet evidenced.
Comparator mechanism documented elsewher: Singapore directly links verified facility reports to carbon tax; China and Korea link verified data to allowance compliance; India links GEI targets to future certificate compliance.
Institutional design option surfaced by: A policy design option is explicit data-use rules that identify which verified dataset controls tax/ETS liability, NDC tracking and policy revision.
